resources.string: A root firewall you can check and undo

RootGuard decides per app whether it may use Wi-Fi, mobile data or VPN, enforced by the Linux kernel through a small root helper. Every change is previewed, applied as a journaled transaction, read back from the kernel to verify it, and can be rolled back.

• Per-app Wi-Fi / mobile / VPN rules, IPv4 and IPv6 • Honest capability check of your kernel and ROM • Verify after apply, automatic compensation on failure • One-tap recovery that removes only RootGuard\'s own rules, offline
Traffic history and behaviour alerts, threat lists, domain rules, tethering, file scanning. These are shown as unsupported, not faked.

Only these typed operations: check capabilities, validate a plan, apply it to its own chain RG_OUT, read it back, roll back, report health, and remove its own rules. It changes only the RG_OUT chain and one jump to it in OUTPUT, for IPv4 and IPv6.
No shell or command input, no SELinux changes, no flushing of Android\'s or other apps\' firewall rules, no certificate interception, no hidden operation.
The installed-app list and your rules stay on this phone. The app has no internet permission. Nothing is backed up to the cloud.
I own this device and allow RootGuard\'s root helper to manage its own firewall rules.
Root access alone does not prove the firewall works on your kernel. This check asks for root, then tests iptables, owner matching and interfaces in a scratch chain that never touches traffic.
RootGuard cannot enforce anything without root. Grant it in your root manager (e.g. Magisk or KernelSU) and check again. Nothing has been changed.
This kernel lacks iptables owner matching, which per-app rules need. RootGuard will not pretend to protect you.
You can change this later. Switching always shows a preview first.
Apps keep internet access; you block the ones you choose.
Apps have no internet unless you allow them. You must allow important apps (store, messaging, system services) yourself.
Mobile data blocked for every app except those you allow; Wi-Fi unchanged.
Observe needs the traffic metadata sensor and Privacy needs vetted tracker lists. Both are later milestones and are not offered yet.
Tap a network to block or allow it for that app. Rules apply to the app\'s UID.
Strict mode: everything is blocked until you allow it. Allow important apps explicitly; RootGuard does not trust any app by its name.
This policy cannot be applied as it is.
RootGuard keeps the last verified rules. A failed apply is compensated back to them; Android\'s own rules are never touched.
Several apps share one UID; the rule affects all of them.
A rule without an app affects every UID, including system services.
Default deny covers app UIDs of this user only:
Isolated and SDK-sandbox processes use other UID ranges and are not covered.
DNS lookups are made by Android\'s resolver, not the app; blocked apps can still resolve names.
Encrypted DNS is not visible to RootGuard.
VPN rules use tun+ and are not yet verified on this device.
IPv6 cannot be enforced on this device; apps may still connect over IPv6.
A temporary override comes before a threat rule.
Another firewall\'s chains were found; both may act on the same traffic:
Whether connections that are already open stop immediately is not yet verified on this device.
Domain rules are not supported yet.
Tethering traffic cannot be filtered yet.
LAN rules cannot be combined with a destination.
No mobile data interface was found. Turn on mobile data and check the device again.
The kernel lacks iptables owner matching.
Strict mode needs IPv6 enforcement, which this device lacks.
Applying and reading back from the kernel…
The kernel now holds exactly the planned rules.
The previous verified rules were restored.
Check the state below. Use recovery if needed.
Enforcement and monitoring are separate. Traffic monitoring is not available yet, so no traffic is shown as clean.
Kernel rules are cleared by a reboot. In this version RootGuard does not start at boot; open it and re-apply. Until then the phone is unfiltered.
An app or attacker with root can change or bypass these rules. RootGuard detects drift when you check, but is not tamper-proof.
Kernel rules match the last verified revision.
Verified, but another rule was inserted before RootGuard\'s hook.
No RootGuard rules in the kernel (for example after a reboot).
Kernel rules differ from the last verified revision.
RootGuard rules exist but no policy is recorded.
Recovery could not remove all RootGuard rules.
An interrupted apply had completed in the kernel and was recorded.
The root helper is not reachable.
Removes only RootGuard\'s chain and hook for IPv4 and IPv6. Android\'s and other apps\' rules stay. Your saved rules are kept and can be applied again.
Root was denied or is not installed.
This firewall backend is not available on the device.
The device check is out of date. Check the device again.
The kernel state changed outside this session. Check against the kernel, or use recovery.
The plan was rejected by validation.
The kernel did not end up with the planned rules.
Restoring the previous rules failed. Use recovery.
The root helper refused the caller.
App and helper versions do not match.
